messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Paging oncall @sheriff_jen: high-rate of GPU driver resets (Xid 79/43) detected in region-us-west-2. Average host flaps: 18/min, multiple containers OOM/killed. Auto-remediation attempted: cordon+drain.

sheriff_jen: on it. pulling up node list and recent flares. which pool is this hitting?

leo: it's mainly hitting rwi-dedicated-gpu-pool-7, nodes: rwi-gpu-0752, rwi-gpu-0753, rwi-gpu-0754. Getting constant nvml Xid entries in dmesg.

toni_ops: I see repeated kernel logs: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79" and container exits with OOM. Cpu/mem not saturated; GPU ECC counters spiking on 0753.

max_ml: customers hitting inference timeouts. Hosted API latency p50 -> p95 spike from 120ms to 1.6s for a subset of routes. Some requests retried and hit quota errors.

linda_infra: cordoned 0753 already. starting graceful drain on 0752/0754 to reduce scheduled work. Will leave 0753 quarantined for now.

leo: running quick check: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=rwi-gpu-0753` -> shows 12 pods evicted, 3 pods restarted repeatedly.

toni_ops: grabbing driver and kernel logs now. pastebin: https://paste.redwood.example/abcd1234 (contains tail -n 200 /var/log/kern.log and nvidia-smi -q output)

linda_infra: nvidia-smi shows ECC volatile counts jumping in the last 5m on 0753 for GPU0 and GPU2, memory errors. Could be thermal or DIMM. hardware team ticket being opened.

leo: quick mitigation: suggest reverting recent driver kernel patch applied yesterday on the 075x nodes? any rollout history?

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-14T22:11:42 -> rollback candidate flagged: service/model-serving-cpu -> rolled to stable 2026-03-14T19:03:11.

max_ml: We should scale down heavy batch jobs and force routing to fallback model variant with lower memory footprint. Can we flip routing for critical routes?

toni_ops: Done — updated routing policy to prefer model-compact-v2 for <=512 token requests. This drops quality slightly but avoids allocating large KV caches.

sean_cs: Notifying affected customers: four active Dedicated tenants saw degraded throughput; one reported 503s. Sent preliminary note and apology; offering status updates.

sheriff_jen: Action plan for next hour: 1) keep 0753 quarantined, 2) drain 0752/0754 and evacuate workloads, 3) try driver restart on a single repro node (0754) after evacuation, 4) if driver restart fails, full node reboot + hardware ticket. Who can execute driver restart?

linda_infra: I can do the restart on 0754. Command sequence: `sudo systemctl stop kubelet && modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia && systemctl start kubelet` then watch dmesg/journal and NVML. Will run on a non-production pod first.

leo: When restarting driver, capture `dmesg -T | tail -n 200` and `sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:03:00.0/information` and `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`.

linda_infra: executing on 0754 in 2m. will post logs.

(5 minutes pass)

linda_infra: driver restart complete on 0754. dmesg shows Xid burst immediately after restart then quieted. ECC counters stable for now. node rejoined cluster.

toni_ops: saw a drop in driver reset rate after 0754 restart. but 0752 still noisy. recommending staggered restarts rather than simultaneous reboots.

max_ml: latency improved for routed requests. still seeing a small bump in error rate (~2% for a few routes). continuing to route to compact model where possible.

sheriff_jen: customer impact summary for handoff: - scope: us-west-2 GPU dedicated pool, ~3 nodes impacted, ~4 Dedicated customers saw degraded throughput, hosted API p95 spike for some endpoints; no data loss. - mitigation: nodes cordoned/drained, staggered driver restart on 0754 succeeded, hardware ticket opened for 0753. - ongoing: monitoring ECC counters, plan to repro with stress test on 0752 in maintenance window.

sean_cs: sending updated customer message now: ETA unknown, mitigation in progress, next update in 30m.

leo: notes for next oncall: check kernel Xid types — 43 often points to GPU access conflicts, 79 is more generic driver fault. collect `nvidia-bug-report.sh` if we need vendor support. escalate to hardware ops if ECC memory errors persist.

linda_infra: created hw-ticket #HW-48912, attached logs and ECC counters, requested priority replacement/inspection for rwi-gpu-0753.

sheriff_jen: handoff checklist for next shift (copy paste): - check incident dashboard (GPU resets > 5/min) - nodes quarantined: rwi-gpu-0753 (open hw ticket) - next steps: 1) run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` on repro node, 2) run targeted memtest if instructed by hw, 3) coordinate with support for customer communication. - escalation: if resets reappear after driver restart on additional nodes, consider rolling capacity to alternate region.

deploy-bot: Reminder: rolling deploy disabled for model-serving for this incident window.

sean_cs: I'll keep customers updated. tagging legal/security if needed.

sheriff_jen: ok team — continuing watch. if error rate stays below 1% for 30m we'll move to monitoring-only and close paging. otherwise escalate. leaving this thread for oncall handoff at 2003456830. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
